hook: SCP-1846 is a short, deadpan file about a middle-aged man covered in living corn leaves who must be kept behind concrete or glass. The procedures look arbitrary at first, from wind-speed sensors outside his cell to a diet of nothing but maize, and the fun is in the interview that explains them. Treat it as a comedy wearing a straight-faced report. The interview includes a few crude jokes.
whyItMatters: The article shows how a single interview can make every odd line of the procedures click into place: the downdraft, the list of acceptable materials, even the threat of corn syrup. It plays an end-of-the-world premise for laughs by pairing a rapture with a god who is confused by modern building materials. The closing reminder to stay skeptical leaves everything as his unverified claim, which is part of the joke.
thingsToNotice: SCP-1846 says he is an angel of Srqnabotf, a corn god whose last worshippers died out after the Spanish arrived, and that lobbying for corn subsidies was his chosen job because grown and eaten corn is what sustains his god. His sudden transformation during a meeting at a senator's home was that god's version of the rapture: the other angels were pulled into the sky from the fields, and the world ends once he is collected too. He is still here only because the god mistakes concrete and glass for gravel and sand, so instead of tearing them apart it keeps blowing on them, which is the 60 to 80 kph downdraft the sensors track. The interview closes on a sales pitch that turns grim, claiming your lot in the afterlife depends on how much corn you grow or use, until the doctor cuts him off mid-sentence about Eurasians who lived before the Columbian Exchange.
